ssmd_version: '0.9'
title: The Printer That Needed Closure
pause_defaults:
  enabled: true
  sentence: 180ms
  paragraph: 450ms
  voice_change: 200ms
---
:::{voice="narrator"}
At nine fifteen on Monday morning, Daniel needed to print one page. One page. A shipping label. He had a meeting in ten minutes, a parcel under one arm, and the confidence of a man who had clearly learned nothing from previous printers.
:::
:::{voice="host"}
Print. ...700ms
:::
:::{voice="narrator"}
The printer blinked. Then it displayed a message.
:::
:::{pitch="high" voice="guest"}
Before printing, please confirm that you are emotionally prepared to use paper.
:::
:::{voice="host"}
Print.
:::
:::{pitch="high" voice="guest"}
Thank you. Would you describe your relationship with paper as positive, neutral, or complicated?
:::
:::{rate="slow" voice="narrator"}
Daniel checked the tray. It was empty. The screen announced, **Paper is ready when you are.**
:::
:::{voice="host" volume="loud"}
I opened it because you told me to check the paper. ...600ms
:::
:::{voice="guest"}
Please read the message aloud.
:::
:::{voice="narrator"}
Daniel stared at it. Then at the parcel. Then back at the printer. ...650ms He picked up a pen and wrote the address by hand.

The printer immediately woke up.
:::
:::{voice="guest"}
Would you like help with handwriting?
:::
